branch_provenance.syndrome: Subacute Progressive Multifocal Neurological Deficit with Extensive Nonenhancing Lesions

state.case_summary:
A woman in her mid-60s presented with episodes of spasms and tremors in her right hand and forearm. She underwent carpal tunnel release surgery initially. The tremors recurred and she was referred to a neurologist 7 months later. Over the subsequent 3 months, she developed progressive right-sided weakness, dysarthria, hand tremors, slurred speech, and gait instability.

No specific physical examination findings were reported in the case.

- Imaging Studies:    1. Initial Brain MRI: T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI showed hyperintensities throughout the bilateral cerebral hemispheric white matter, corpus callosum, basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, upper pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles.    2. T1-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery MRI with contrast showed absence of contrast enhancement.    Image Title: Extensive Nonenhancing Lesions in the Bilateral Cerebral Hemispheres    Image Description: A) Diffuse T2-weighted FLAIR MRI reveals hyperintensities in the white matter and corpus callosum, extending to the basal ganglia, thalami, midbrain, pons, and middle cerebellar peduncles. B) T1-weighted FLAIR MRI with contrast reveals absence of contrast enhancement.  - Pathological Tests:    1. Brain Biopsy (left frontal lesion): CD5− CD10− CD19+ CD20+ BCL6+ MUM-1+ EBV/EBER−    2. Cytogenetic study: Normal female karyotype    3. Fluorescence in situ hybridization: Extra copies of BCL6 (3q27) and BCL2 (18q21), no MYC abnormalities    4. Cerebrospinal fluid: Presence of lymphoma cells    5. Bone marrow: Negative for lymphoma cells

What is the most likely diagnosis?

Options:
A. Primary central nervous system lymphoma (PCNSL)
B. Intravascular large B-cell lymphoma
C. Secondary CNS involvement by systemic diffuse large B-cell lymphoma
D. Lymphomatosis cerebri variant of diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL)

alarm_features: Presence of lymphoma cells in cerebrospinal fluid
excluded_candidates: Ischemic stroke: unlikely due to absence of contrast enhancement and presence of lymphoma cells
Infectious process: unlikely due to absence of contrast enhancement and presence of lymphoma cells
Demyelinating disease: possible, but less likely due to presence of lymphoma cells and extra copies of BCL6 and BCL2
